QF.id: SIA Social Stock Exchange Introduction and Instruments_25

question.text: In the 'Pay-for-success through Grants' structure (Figure 2.3), if the NPO achieves the pre-defined outcomes, the CSR funder typically releases the escrowed capital as follows:

answer.text: Partly to the interim funding partner (to cover its cost of implementing the programme) and partly to the NPO in the form of an accelerator grant up to 10% of the programme cost if the NPO exceeds the pre-defined outcome targets.
100% is paid to the NPO as a grant, and the interim funding partner writes off its contribution.
The CSR capital is rolled over to the next year regardless of performance.
The full amount is returned to the CSR donor.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook p.63, upon verified achievement of outcomes the CSR funder pays the escrowed capital partly to the interim funding partner (to cover its cost of implementing the programme) and partly to the NPO in the form of an accelerator grant up to 10% of the programme cost where the NPO exceeds the pre-defined outcome targets. The Trap: Option B describes the non-completion rollover scenario, not success — it incorrectly omits the interim funding partner's repayment claim. Option C describes a rollover rather than a successful release. Option D would defeat the purpose of the structure. Note: The accelerator grant component (up to 10%) is conditional on exceeding the pre-defined outcome targets.
